articles.description:
RAG chatbots fail silently.
Imagine you've hired a chatbot to handle FAQs on your behalf, so you can level up your D&D character instead of replying to the same questions over and over. You provided all the information you could think of.
Then your potential biggest client asks if you're left or right handed. The chatbot doesn't know. The client walks away. It never occurred to you to teach it. Who asks that? You will never know. Because you had no idea there was a missed question in the first place.
In this tutorial, we're building an MCP server that creates that feedback loop. When the chatbot gives a low-confidence answer, it logs the question. Over time, questions pile up. Run the pattern analysis and it clusters them by semantic similarity — "oh, 40 people asked about refund policies …

articles.description:
A state in the US just enshrined computation as a constitutional right. And the tech world is split on whether it's genius or pure nightmare fuel.
Senate Bill 212, or the "Right to Compute Act," was signed into law in April 2025. It establishes that your right to own and use computational resources — that's hardware, software, AI tools, servers — should be considered a fundamental liberty. Just like freedom of speech.
Any government prohibition on computation is now required to be "demonstrably necessary and narrowly tailored." The same legal test you have to meet to restrict free speech. It's intense.
The Hacker News thread on this is currently trending at 243 points, and boy, the comments are salty.
Most state proposals for regulating AI lately are basically trying to limit the kinds of …
articles.title: Montana Made Computation a Constitutional Right. Devs Are Split.

RLAAS (Rate Limiting As A Service) is an open-source, policy-driven platform for controlling HTTP traffic, logs, spans, metrics, and events with one reusable engine.
Every engineering team knows they need rate limiting. But most solutions only protect one layer — the API gateway.
What happens to everything else?
Here are the real pain points I kept running into:
Log floods — A bug sends millions of error logs to your observability stack. Costs spike. Dashboards break. On-call engineers drown in noise.
Metric storms — A chatty service emits 50x normal Datadog metrics during a deployment. Your bill triples overnight.
Kafka cascades — A slow consumer falls behind. Retries pile up. One service takes down the entire event pipeline.
Sidecar blindspots — Traffic between services inside a mesh nev…
articles.title: RLAAS (Rate Limiting As A Service): Rate Limiting Across Modern Systems

articles.author: Marina Kovalchuk
articles.description:
Introduction: The AI Paradox


Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the workplace is a double-edged sword. On one edge, it slashes through inefficiencies, automating repetitive tasks and accelerating project timelines. Mechanistically, AI-driven automation reduces the time required for task completion by 30-50%, as observed in manufacturing and data processing sectors. This efficiency surge, however, triggers a productivity paradox: management, armed with faster tools, recalibrates expectations upward. The causal chain is clear: AI’s speed → increased output capacity → higher productivity demands. Employees, now capable of completing tasks in half the time, are assigned double the workload. This deformation of workload norms is the first crack in the system, widening the gap between human capac…
articles.title: AI Integration in Workplaces Causes Burnout: Strategies to Mitigate Overwork and Protect Employee Well-being
